title: Consequences Of The Tech IPO Boom

Consequences Of The Tech IPO Boom

Thomas Gatley

Gavekal Dragonomics | 31 Jul 2026

Initial public offerings by Chinese companies have been on a tear this year, a trend capped by the blockbuster debut of memory-chip maker CXMT Corp. on the Shanghai STAR market this week. CXMT raised at least RMB58bn—the biggest fundraising on Chinese markets since Alibaba’s RMB91bn secondary listing in Hong Kong in 2019—and total IPO activity so far this year, both onshore and offshore, is running more than double last year’s pace.For those familiar with Chinese market and macro history, such a surge in fundraising raises two concerns. First, that the withdrawal of market liquidity will mark the end of the upward trend in Chinese equities since 2024, as has happened so often in the past. Second, that this surge of cash will herald a new wave of capital expenditures and a worsening of excess capacity. How big are these potential after-effects from Chinese technology firms cashing in on market enthusiasm?
